items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: They'll holler, Tom Seaver. Well, Tom Seaver gets hit, but if there wasn't somebody out there to catch that ball and throw it...

ctx.x: we came back. Where musicians set there and built plans and dreamed. Of course, your breakfast would always consist of an order of hotcakes, two pork chops and three scrambled eggs and coffee and things like that. Of course, some of the boys would drink, but I didn't bother with much of that. But that was the breakfast. That's what was served. Hotcakes and maybe three scrambled eggs and some sausage and potatoes and -- french fried potatoes or home fried potatoes. Well, you see, but when we sit there, that's…

and go through. Well, you used to be getting the ball. So, I mean, but everybody -- which is very wrong, even with a baseball team. They'll holler, Tom Seaver. Well, Tom Seaver gets hit, but if there wasn't somebody out there to catch that ball and throw it, when you have a no-hit game, for instance. You have struck out everybody, but the man -- your supporting cast. I think it's very wrong that the newspapers come out and say, 'Tom Seaver did this.' Or it's very wrong to do that.
